body:
### Summary

uv can intermittently quit with an error code and no error message. I've seeing it on windows specifically, and have reproduced it 16/1000 times on uv 0.13.4, and 0/1000 times with a patched 0.13.4 build. The patched build of uv 0.13.4, with `AWS_LC_SYS_NO_JITTER_ENTROPY=1` set, worked around an issue in https://github.com/aws/aws-lc, which is as a transient dependency to uv via aws-lc-rs which in turn is transient via rustls.

The foundational issue is related to unreliable acquisition of sufficiently random numbers, as needed for web requests.

Let me know if you want help verifying its fixed in some uv build! I'm attaching an AI generated report about it as well for more details.

### Related upstream issues

- Upstream issue, represented in aws-lc: aws/aws-lc#3604
- Upstream issue, represented in aws-lc-rs: aws/aws-lc-rs#1072
- Upstream issue fix: aws/aws-lc#3631

### Related uv issues

- The issue has surfaced without windows involved before it seems: astral-sh/uv#21743

### AI writeup

<details><summary>Technical AI writeup</summary>

### Summary

On a Windows 11 VM, `uv` sometimes exits with `0xC0000409` (`-1073740791`) and prints nothing. It happens in any command that opens an HTTPS connection (`uv sync`, `uv tool run --with …`, `uv build`, `uv pip compile`), and a rerun passes. The cause is aws-lc's CPU-jitter entropy setup calling `abort()` during the first `RAND_bytes` of the TLS handshake: `jent_entropy_collector_alloc()` returns NULL in `tree_jitter_initialize_once` (`tree_drbg_jitter_entropy.c:270`, aws-lc-sys 0.44.0).

We can reproduce it on demand: with one file-churning process per CPU, about 3% of fresh `uv pip compile --refresh` runs abort. Offline runs and runs without the load never abort.

This looks like `aws/aws-lc-rs#1072`, which also includes a uv stack (0.11.x, VMware). This report adds a cheap reproduction, confirmation on the latest uv (0.13.4), and which allocation fails.

### Environment

- uv 0.13.4 (`7456b60bc 2026-10-20 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), the official release zip. It also happens with 0.11.0 and 0.11.33, i.e. every release since aws-lc replaced ring.
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, a QEMU/KVM guest (`Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009)`, `HypervisorPresent: True`), 4 vCPUs on an AMD Ryzen 5 3600 host, a QEMU virtual disk.
- The process runs as SYSTEM, from a GitLab Runner shell executor. Defender real-time protection is on, with the working dir and uv's cache excluded.

### Reproduction

Run the script below from an empty directory on a Windows VM. It writes only under `.\uv-abort-repro` (cache and a managed Python included):

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File repro-uv-jitter-abort.ps1 -Uv C:\path\to\uv.exe -Iterations 150
```

<details><summary>repro-uv-jitter-abort.ps1</summary>

```powershell
# Reproduces uv exiting with 0xC0000409 (aws-lc jitter entropy abort) on a
# Windows VM: one file-churning process per CPU, while a fresh uv process
# makes one HTTPS request at a time. Run from an empty directory:
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File repro-uv-jitter-abort.ps1 [-Uv uv.exe] [-Iterations 150]
param([string] $Uv = "uv", [int] $Iterations = 150)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$work = (New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$PWD\uv-abort-repro").FullName
$env:UV_CACHE_DIR = "$work\cache"
$env:UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR = "$work\python"
$env:RUST_LOG = "uv=debug,rustls=debug"
Set-Content "$work\req.in" "iniconfig"
& $Uv python install 3.12 --quiet
$python = (& $Uv python find 3.12 --managed-python)

# Disk load: create, fsync, read back and delete files in a loop.
Set-Content "$work\churn.py" @'
import os, shutil, sys, tempfile
root = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=sys.argv[1]); blob = os.urandom(1 << 20)
while True:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=root)
    for i in range(200):
        with open(os.path.join(d, f"{i}.bin"), "wb") as f: f.write(blob[: 4096 * (i % 64 + 1)])
    with open(os.path.join(d, "big.bin"), "wb") as f:
        for _ in range(64): f.write(blob)
        f.flush(); os.fsync(f.fileno())
    for n in os.listdir(d):
        with open(os.path.join(d, n), "rb") as f: f.read()
    shutil.rmtree(d)
'@
$churn = @(1..[int]$env:NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS | ForEach-Object {
    Start-Process $python -ArgumentList "-I", "$work\churn.py", $work -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden })
try {
    $crashes = 0
    foreach ($i in 1..$Iterations) {
        $p = Start-Process $Uv -ArgumentList "pip", "compile", "$work\req.in", "--python", $python, "--refresh", "--no-header" `
            -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru -RedirectStandardError "$work\last.log" -RedirectStandardOutput "$work\out.txt"
        if ($p.ExitCode -eq -1073740791) {
            $crashes++
            Write-Host "run $i exited 0xC0000409; last log lines:"
            Get-Content "$work\last.log" -Tail 3 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $_" }
        }
    }
    Write-Host "$crashes of $Iterations runs exited 0xC0000409"
}
finally {
    $churn | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
```
</details>

Results on the VM above (uv 0.13.4, 4 churn processes):

| Runs | Disk load | Network | Exit 0xC0000409 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uv pip compile --refresh` (one HTTPS request) | yes | online | 4 / 100, 3 / 150, 5 / 150 |
| same, `--offline` (warm cache, no TLS) | yes | offline | 0 / 100 |
| same, `--refresh` | no | online | 0 / 100 |
| standalone script above | yes | online | 3 / 150 |

With `RUST_LOG=uv=debug,rustls=debug`, every crash ends at the same point, right after the TCP connect and before the ClientHello:

```
DEBUG connecting to 151.101.192.223:443
DEBUG connected to 151.101.192.223:443
DEBUG No cached session for DnsName("pypi.org")
DEBUG Not resuming any session
```

The Windows crash record (event 1000 / WER `BEX64`) names `uv.exe` itself as the faulting module, with exception `0xc0000409`, fail-fast code 7 (`FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT`), offset `0x9d2975` in 0.13.4. The UCRT is statically linked, which is why uv.exe is the "module". `abort()` in a release UCRT prints nothing, and a fail-fast skips uv's unhandled-exception filter, which is why there is no output at all.

### Stack (uv 0.13.4)

No PDBs are published (`astral-sh/uv#20632`), so we caught the fail-fast under a debugger (Win32 debug API plus `StackWalk64`, which unwinds with the exe's `.pdata`). It was identical in all 8 captured crashes. We named frames by disassembling the release `uv.exe`: the 9 `jent_*` functions it exports, the source paths of the panic locations each function references, and the aws-lc-sys 0.44.0 source.

```
 0 uv.exe+0x9d2975   ucrt abort()                       (int 0x29, ecx=7)
 1 uv.exe+0x98fdb0   tree_jitter_initialize_once        tree_drbg_jitter_entropy.c:270
 2 uv.exe+0x996ff6   call_once_init                     thread_win.c
 3 ntdll.dll+0x788e5 RtlRunOnceExecuteOnce
 4 KERNELBASE.dll+0xb30f1 InitOnceExecuteOnce
 5 uv.exe+0x996ece   CRYPTO_once
 6 uv.exe+0x949fde   tree_jitter_initialize
 7 uv.exe+0x989c9d   (get_entropy_source / rand_state_initialize)
 8 uv.exe+0x936d23   (RAND_bytes)
 9 uv.exe+0x21e16f   (aws_lc_rs::rand::fill)
10 uv.exe+0x22713c   rustls client handshake            rustls-0.23.45/src/client/hs.rs
11 uv.exe+0x1ecd99   reqwest connector                  reqwest-0.13.4/src/async_impl/client.rs
   … hyper, astral-reqwest-retry, uv-client/src/middleware.rs, uv-client/src/retry.rs, uv-resolver, tokio …
42 ntdll.dll+0x7ee4c RtlUserThreadStart
```

Frames 7–9 are inferred from their position between `CRYPTO_once` and rustls, not from their content. Frame 1 is certain. `0x98fcd0` allocates 0x150 bytes, calls `jent_entropy_collector_alloc`, then `tree_jitter_get_root_seed` (`0x98fc30`, which has its own `abort()`s that are not on the stack), then `CTR_DRBG_init`. Its three failure branches share the one `abort()` call at `0x98fdab`.

To tell the branches apart, we read the frame's non-volatile `rbx` (the new `tree_jitter_drbg_t`) after unwinding. In 5 of 5 crashes `rbx` is a valid heap pointer and `jitter_ec` (`[rbx+0x148]`) is NULL. So the zalloc succeeded and `jent_entropy_collector_alloc(0, JENT_FORCE_FIPS)` returned NULL, which is line 270. (That allocation runs jitterentropy's timing health tests. Our assumption is that they fail because of timer noise in a busy VM; we haven't observed that directly.)

### Ruled out

- **Not a panic, stack overflow, or OOM in Rust code:** each of those prints a message first. The fault offset is the UCRT `abort()` (`IsProcessorFeaturePresent(PF_FASTFAIL_AVAILABLE)` → `int 0x29`, fallback `0x40000015`), and the caller is aws-lc C code.
- **Not file I/O in uv itself:** the same command with `--offline` under the same load never crashes. `UV_LINK_MODE=copy` doesn't help either; our CI already sets it.
- **Not CPU load alone:** CPU-only load didn't reproduce it in our earlier trials. Disk churn does.
- **Probably not antivirus:** the working directory and uv's cache are excluded from Defender, and the abort is a failed timing health test, not a file operation. We haven't tried with real-time protection off.
- **Not version-specific:** 0.11.0, 0.11.33 and 0.13.4 all fail the same way.

### Fix, tested

Building the Windows binary with `AWS_LC_SYS_NO_JITTER_ENTROPY=1`, so aws-lc seeds from `ProcessPrng`/`BCryptGenRandom` instead (the workaround suggested in `aws/aws-lc-rs#1072`), removes the crash in our reproduction:

| 1,000 rounds each, interleaved, same disk load | Exit 0xC0000409 | Exit 0 |
|---|---|---|
| uv 0.13.4 built with `AWS_LC_SYS_NO_JITTER_ENTROPY=1` | 0 | 1000 |
| official uv 0.13.4 release | 16 | 984 |

One-sided Fisher exact test: p = 1.4e-5 (criterion fixed beforehand: 0 crashes and p < 0.01). Upper 95% bound on the patched build's crash rate: 0.3%.

The patched build is uv 0.13.4 (`7456b60bc`) cross-compiled with clang/lld: `--release --locked --features self-update,windows-gui-bin`, static CRT as in the release, but no PGO and no LTO. An otherwise identical build with jitter entropy left on also crashed (4 / 400, alongside 5 / 400 for the official release and 0 / 400 for the patched build in a three-way run), so the difference is the jitter setting, not the build setup.

Alternatively, pick up `aws/aws-lc#3631` ("Recover from CPU Jitter failures in non-FIPS builds", open) once it reaches aws-lc-sys.

Related: `aws/aws-lc-rs#1072`, `aws/aws-lc#3604`, `aws/aws-lc#3631`, `astral-sh/uv#20632`, `astral-sh/uv#21743` (same class of abort on aarch64, RNDR).

</details>

### Platform

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, x86_64 (QEMU/KVM virtual machine, 4 vCPUs)

### Version

uv 0.13.4

### Python version

Python 3.12.15
title: Intermittent silent exit with an error code - related to transient aws-lc dependency
